# Results — Study 489 (Chaikin Oscillator)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The believers' claim — **A/D
momentum leads price: when EMA3(ADL) − EMA10(ADL) crosses above zero, accumulation is building
and price is about to rise** — encoded as a mechanical rule. The oscillator is the standard
EMA(3) − EMA(10) of the Accumulation/Distribution line; a long fires on the first bar whose
oscillator turns from ≤ 0 to > 0 (read on the close of t), entered at the **next close** (one
documented lag), and we measure the forward 5/10/20/60-day return. Offline & deterministic once
cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted (**total-return**) closes for **SPY, QQQ, IWM, DIA, GLD** (public, no key) |
| Window | 2005-01-03 → 2026-05-29 (**As-of 2026-05-31**, partial June dropped; **21.4** years) |
| SPY fingerprint | `4cb5244f3990` (sha1[:12] of the close column, As-of slice) |
| Entries | **1452** mechanical cross-above-zero signals pooled across the 5 tapes (EMA 3/10) |
| Volume | shared cache stores OHLC only → a **deterministic, look-ahead-free** range-based volume proxy feeds the ADL (see [`data._proxy_volume`](../chaikin_oscillator/data.py)) |
| Timing / costs | EMAs causal (past-only), warm-up = 10 bars; cross read on close of t, enter the **next close** (one lag); hold 5/10/20/60 days; **1 bp** one-way × 2 legs per signal |

> **Price-only vs total-return.** The ETFs are auto-adjusted (dividends reinvested) — labelled
> total-return everywhere. The Signal axis uses a basket of **surviving** liquid ETFs; this is a
> single-instrument momentum study, not a cross-sectional anomaly, so survivorship affects only
> the drift baseline (which is exactly what the random-entry control neutralizes).
>
> **Volume caveat.** The Chaikin oscillator needs volume, which the shared price-pattern cache
> does not store. The proxy is a monotone function of the bar's range (`high-low`) using only
> current-bar data, so it leaks no future information; it is a faithful-enough stand-in for the
> *shape* of the indicator and cannot fabricate a price lead. The placebo and random baseline
> neutralize it either way.

## The signal — cross-above-zero vs a drift-matched random baseline (the honest test)

One-sample *t* is the **misleading** number (it measures the index's upward drift); the
**Welch cross-vs-random** *t* is the test that matters. Δ = cross − random.

| horizon | n | cross | win% | one-sample *t* | random | Δ (cross−random) | net of cost | Welch *t* | *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5-day  | 1452 | +22.4 bps | 57% | +3.03 | +28.3 bps | **−5.9 bps** | +20.4 bps | −0.56 | 0.575 |
| 10-day | 1451 | +41.0 bps | 60% | +3.63 | +63.2 bps | **−22.3 bps** | +39.0 bps | −1.65 | 0.099 |
| 20-day | 1449 | +96.0 bps | 63% | +4.88 | +117.9 bps | **−21.9 bps** | +94.0 bps | −1.14 | 0.254 |
| 60-day | 1444 | +278.6 bps | 67% | +5.81 | +348.4 bps | **−69.8 bps** | +276.6 bps | −2.14 | 0.032 |

Read it carefully. The one-sample *t* against zero looks spectacular (**+4.88** at 20 days,
**+5.81** at 60) — but that is **pure beta**: long-only entries on an upward-drifting index
inherit the drift. Against the **drift-matched random baseline**, the cross-above-zero entry is
*worse* at **every** horizon (Δ = −5.9 / −22.3 / −21.9 / −69.8 bps), and at 60 days it is
*significantly worse* than random (Welch *t* = **−2.14**, *p* = 0.032 — the cross actively
**underperforms** a dart). The cross-minus-random difference is never positive, let alone above
the desk's *t* ≥ 2 bar. A/D momentum does not lead price.

## Per-ticker (H = 20) — the cross loses to random almost everywhere

| ticker | entries | cross | one-sample *t* | random | Δ (cross−random) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY | 272 | +80.4 bps | +2.03 | +131.1 bps | **−50.7 bps** |
| QQQ | 270 | +137.3 bps | +3.17 | +129.4 bps | **+7.9 bps** |
| IWM | 322 | +112.3 bps | +2.28 | +120.6 bps | **−8.3 bps** |
| DIA | 289 | +49.9 bps | +1.31 | +102.6 bps | **−52.6 bps** |
| GLD | 299 | +99.4 bps | +2.71 | +107.4 bps | **−8.0 bps** |

Only **QQQ** edges out a positive delta (+7.9 bps); in 4 of 5 names the Chaikin cross
*underperforms* a dart-throwing entry. No coherent cross-sectional edge — the hallmark of
relabelled drift.

## Geometry placebo — scramble the A/D readings, nothing changes

The decisive "does the A/D geometry matter?" test: keep the **marginal** Money Flow Multiplier
distribution and the **volume** intact, but permute *which day's accumulation reading* sits on
which bar, so the cumulated ADL becomes geometric nonsense. If A/D momentum genuinely led price,
the scramble would collapse the result.

| test | observed cross-above-zero 20d return | placebo *p* | draws |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY scrambled-MFM oscillator | +80.4 bps | **0.703** | 500 |

**70% of scrambled-MFM oscillators match or beat the real one** (*p* = 0.703). The accumulation
information carries no forecasting power — a cumulated shuffle of the same readings does just as
well. "A/D momentum leads price" is busted.

## Synthetic positive control — the harness CAN bank a real A/D lead

On a deterministic tape with a *planted* accumulation-leads-price effect (knob `edge`: volume
spikes near the highs followed by a real forward drift), the same cross-above-zero rule behaves
exactly as it must — so the flat real-tape result is a genuine "nothing there", not a dead detector.

| planted edge | n | cross | win% | one-sample *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.00** (no lead) | 222 | −14.0 bps | 48% | −0.37 |
| **0.15** (real planted A/D lead) | 136 | +538.7 bps | 88% | **+16.31** |

With no planted lead the control sits at *t* ≈ 0 (no false positive); a real planted A/D lead
lights up at *t* = +16.31 with an 88% win-rate. The detector is live.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The cross-above-zero entry does **not** beat a drift-matched random baseline
  (cross − random = −5.9 / −22.3 / −21.9 / −69.8 bps at 5/10/20/60 days; the cross-vs-random
  Welch *t* is never positive and is *significantly negative* at 60 days, −2.14, *p* = 0.032).
  The impressive one-sample *t*'s (20-day +4.88, 60-day +5.81) are pure beta — the upward drift
  of long equity indices.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** There is no residual edge once the drift you were always getting is
  removed, and costs only deepen the hole. The same drift is captured more cheaply and more fully
  by holding the index; the cross rule trades less and pays costs on each signal, dominating
  nothing. No capacity question because there is no edge to scale.
- **"Does A/D momentum lead price"? — BUSTED.** The scrambled-MFM placebo leaves the result intact
  (*p* = 0.703): cumulated-nonsense oscillators do as well as the real one, so the specific
  accumulation/distribution geometry carries no forecasting information. The Chaikin oscillator is
  a descriptive momentum overlay, not a leading indicator.
